q: A string fixed at both ends vibrates at its third natural frequency. How many nodes and how many antinodes does the string have, counting the ends?
a: Three half wavelengths fit on the string, so it has three antinodes and four nodes: two at the ends and two between them.

q: A flute is a tube open at both ends and a clarinet roughly a tube closed at one end. The instruments are equally long. Which has the lower fundamental frequency, and how many times as great is the fundamental frequency of the other?
a: The clarinet. The fundamental frequency of a closed tube is $\tfrac{v}{4L}$ and that of an open tube $\tfrac{v}{2L}$, so the fundamental frequency of a flute of the same length is twice as great, that is, an octave higher.
